title: Rate Premium on Holder Refunds Released Late
content:
**Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda — rate premium on holder refunds released late**

A refund released to the holder carries a premium on the yearly rate at which holder late interest runs, set by the calendar days from the effective date of the waiver's ending (the waiver's closing date, day 0) to the release date. The premium is added to the interest rate before the holder late interest is figured.

| Release date, days after the effective date | Premium added to the interest rate |
|---|---|
| More than 45 | 0.02 |
| 21 to 45 | 0.01 |
| Within 20 | None |

**Edges.** Day 20: none. Day 21: 0.01. Day 45: 0.01. Day 46: 0.02.

**Basis Q&A**

*Is the premium measured from the start of the late window?* No. It is measured from the effective date of the waiver's ending, whatever day the late window starts.

*How does the premium enter the interest?* As a yearly rate added to the interest rate: a release whose interest rate is 0.05 and that is made on day 50 runs at 0.07.

**Hypothetical example.** A holder refund of 472.80 is released on day 33 after the effective date, with 3 late days and an interest rate of 0.05. The premium is 0.01, so the interest runs at 0.06: 472.80 times 0.06 times 3, divided by 365, is 0.2331…, rounded half up to 0.23.
